name: Battle of Arrays
description: Alice and Bob play a turn-based game. Initially, Alice has an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ positive integers, and Bob has an array $$$b$$$ of $$$m$$$ positive integers. The players take turns, with Alice moving first. On a player's turn, they must choose one element $$$x$$$ from their own array and the maximal element $$$y$$$ from their opponent's array. Then they perform the following operation: If $$$y \leq x$$$: the element $$$y$$$ is destroyed (removed from the opponent's array). If $$$y \gt x$$$: the element $$$y$$$ is decreased by $$$x$$$ (the value of $$$y$$$ becomes $$$y - x$$$). A player wins if, after their move, the opponent's array becomes empty. Assuming both players play optimally, determine the winner.
input_specification: Each input contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^5$$$). The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$1 \le n,m \le 10^5$$$) — the sizes of Alice's and Bob's arrays respectively. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — Alice's array. The third line contains $$$m$$$ integers $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m$$$ ($$$1 \le b_i \le 10^9$$$) — Bob's array. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$ and the sum of $$$m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the name of the winner of the game if both players follow the optimal strategy: " Alice " or " Bob ".
subsubtopic: 472. Grundy Number and Basic Game Theory
approach_summary: Compute Sprague-Grundy values g(u) = mex({g(v) : u -> v}). Game state is winning iff XOR sum of independent game components is non-zero.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2181B — Battle of Arrays [472. Grundy Number and Basic Game Theory]
topic_editorial.summary: Impartial game theory via Sprague-Grundy theorem.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any finite, impartial game under normal play convention is equivalent to a one-pile game of Nim with pile size equal to its Grundy value $g(u) = \text{mex}(\{g(v) : u \to v\})$. A compound game of independent subgames is winning for the first player if and only if $\bigoplus_{i} g_i \ne 0$.
